vibe: Photographers and wildlife fans sharing jeeps - safaris throw solo travellers together
hub: Fly to Nagpur (NAG), then 2.5-3h drive to Moharli or Kolara gate

name: Loktak Lake
tagline: Floating phumdi islands, world's only floating park

why.winter: Best season — clear water, migratory birds, easiest sangai deer sightings on the phumdis.
why.summer: March-April still good for boating; by May it turns hot and humid ahead of the rains.
why.monsoon: The lake floods significantly, phumdis break loose and drift, park access often restricted.
why.autumn: October water is still settling post-monsoon, boat trips resume through the month.

vibe: Quiet stilted fishing villages; check current travel advisories before going.
hub: Fly Imphal, 1h drive to Moirang. ILP + PAP; check advisories.

name: Cherrapunji (Sohra)
tagline: Wettest place on earth — waterfalls, canyons, caves

why.winter: Dry and clear, good canyon and Nohkalikai Falls views, though the water flow itself is thin.
why.summer: Warming up, waterfalls still decent, dry trails good for root-bridge treks before the rains.
why.monsoon: Holds the world rainfall record here — dramatic falls but near-zero visibility and landslide-shut roads.
why.autumn: Sweet spot — monsoon just broke, falls are at their fullest, skies finally clearing.

vibe: Small Khasi villages, guesthouse guides, same trekkers doing the falls circuit.
hub: 1.5h shared taxi from Shillong (3h from Guwahati). No ILP.

name: Dawki & Shnongpdeng
tagline: Glass-clear Umngot river — boating, cliff camps, border

why.winter: Peak clarity — the Umngot turns glass-clear turquoise, boats look like they float on air.
why.summer: March-April still fairly clear; by May pre-monsoon showers start muddying the river.
why.monsoon: River runs brown and fast, most camps shut down — skip this window entirely.
why.autumn: October water is still settling from monsoon silt, better from November onward.

vibe: River-camp bonfires, kayaking by day, cheap tents by the water, easy to meet people.
hub: 2h shared taxi from Shillong, 4-5h from Guwahati. No ILP.

name: Mawlynnong
tagline: Asia's cleanest village — root bridge, bamboo skywalk

why.winter: Dry paths, clear skies — the Sky View bamboo tower shows Bangladesh's plains below.
why.summer: Warm, green, fewer tourists, though afternoon showers creep in by May.
why.monsoon: Some of India's heaviest rain falls right here — leeches, slick paths, zero views.
why.autumn: October is transitional — trails drying out, village looking its lush best.

vibe: Homestay evenings with Khasi families, mostly day-trippers, quiet overnight stays.
hub: 1h from Dawki, 2.5h shared taxi from Shillong. No ILP.

name: Nongriat (Double-Decker Root Bridge)
tagline: 3,500 steps down to a living double-decker root bridge

why.winter: Dry stone steps make the descent and climb back up far safer, cool weather helps.
why.summer: Doable but humid, steps get slicker as May turns toward the monsoon.
why.monsoon: Steps become a waterslide, genuinely dangerous plus leeches — most guesthouses say skip it.
why.autumn: Rainbow Falls swimming hole still full from monsoon, steps drying out nicely.

vibe: Riverside guesthouses full of trekkers, communal dinners, easy to find company.
hub: Drive to Tyrna (1h from Cherrapunji), trek 3,500 steps down. No ILP.

name: Shillong
tagline: Northeast's hill capital — cafes, lakes, live music

why.winter: Peak season — crisp clear days, misty mornings, easy walks around Ward's Lake without rain gear.
why.summer: Warm and pleasant before the rains hit, greener hills, noticeably fewer tourists than winter.
why.monsoon: City itself copes fine, but day trips to Cherrapunji get washed out and landslides can shut roads.
why.autumn: Best window — monsoon just ended, waterfalls still full, skies clearing fast, comfortable temps.

vibe: Cafe crowd and shared taxis — easy to link up with travellers heading onward.
hub: Fly/bus to Guwahati, then 3h shared taxi to Shillong. No ILP.
festival: Nov: Shillong Cherry Blossom Festival

name: Aizawl
tagline: Mizoram's hillside capital — churches, cafes, rock music

why.winter: Best weather — cool, dry, clear views across the hill ridges the city is built on.
why.summer: Warm and pleasant into April, then humidity builds fast as the rains approach.
why.monsoon: Sits in one of India's wettest monsoon belts — daily downpours, occasional landslides.
why.autumn: October skies clear up nicely, a good shoulder window with fewer visitors.

vibe: Church-going, coffee-shop city — safe and welcoming, small traveller scene.
hub: Fly to Lengpui airport, 40min out. ILP + PAP.
festival: Early Mar: Chapchar Kut spring festival

name: Reiek
tagline: Ridge-top village with hiking trails and border views

why.winter: Clearest ridge views, cool hiking weather, best season to see the peak's rock formations.
why.summer: Pleasant into April, green hillsides, then humidity builds toward the rains.
why.monsoon: Same wet Mizoram monsoon belt as Aizawl — trails turn slick, views vanish into cloud.
why.autumn: October is a good reset after the rains, hiking trails dry out again.

vibe: Half-day escape from Aizawl — cultural-village shows, mostly domestic day-trippers.
hub: 1h drive from Aizawl. ILP + PAP for foreigners.

name: Dzukou Valley
tagline: Rolling green trekking valley famous for summer lilies

why.winter: Cold and frost-covered, grass turns brown, but skies stay clear — pack warm layers.
why.summer: Dry-season trekking, brown rather than green, but trails are safe and views are clear.
why.monsoon: The famous Dzukou lilies bloom in June-July, but you'll fight mud, leeches and fog for it.
why.autumn: The sweet spot — late blooms linger, then the valley turns lush green with the clearest views.

vibe: Trekking-hut camaraderie — shared meals cooked over a wood stove with fellow hikers.
hub: From Kohima: 1h drive + 3-4h trek from Viswema. ILP covers it.

name: Kohima
tagline: Naga hill capital and gateway to Hornbill Festival

why.winter: December is peak — Hornbill Festival packs Kisama; January-February stay cool and clear too.
why.summer: Pleasant hill-station warmth through May, comfortable temperatures, fewer crowds than festival time.
why.monsoon: Heavy rain on steep hill roads brings regular landslides around the district.
why.autumn: October-November is lovely, clear skies building toward December's festival crowds.

vibe: Hornbill month is a huge friendly crowd; otherwise a quiet WWII-history town.
hub: Fly Dimapur, 3h shared taxi to Kohima. ILP + PAP.
festival: Dec 1-10: Hornbill Festival, Kisama Village

name: Chilika Lake (Satapada)
tagline: Asia's largest lagoon — dolphins and migratory birds

why.winter: The only season worth the trip — dolphins more active, Nalabana fills with migratory birds.
why.summer: Water levels drop and heat makes open boat rides uncomfortable; dolphin sightings get harder.
why.monsoon: Freshwater inflow clouds the lagoon and rough water makes dolphin boats unreliable.
why.autumn: Oct is a quieter early option; birds and dolphins are still building toward the winter peak.

vibe: Day-trip crowd from Puri - sharing a dolphin boat is the easiest way to meet people.
hub: 1.5hr drive from Puri to Satapada jetty for boat tours.

name: Daringbadi
tagline: 'Kashmir of Odisha' — pine forests, frost, coffee gardens

why.winter: The whole reason to come — frost most mornings, occasional snow, genuinely cold for Odisha.
why.summer: Cooler than the plains but still warm by midday; waterfalls run thin until the rains arrive.
why.monsoon: Waterfalls run full and the forest turns lush, but ghat roads get landslide-prone and slick.
why.autumn: Pleasant and green post-monsoon, with the first hints of winter chill by late November.

vibe: Barely any tourist infrastructure - mostly Kandha villagers, not backpackers.
hub: 7hr drive from Bhubaneswar via Phulbani; own vehicle recommended.

name: Gopalpur
tagline: Sleepy colonial beach town, quiet alternative to Puri

why.winter: Quiet, cool and empty — the best months for walking the lighthouse beach without Puri crowds.
why.summer: Increasingly hot and humid through May; the beach empties out almost entirely.
why.monsoon: Rough seas and heavy rain make the beach unusable for most of the season.
why.autumn: Weather turns pleasant by November; October can still carry monsoon leftovers.

vibe: Old lighthouse, empty sand, not much else after dark - solitude, not a scene.
hub: Nearest hub Berhampur, 30min auto; 6hr from Bhubaneswar.

name: Konark
tagline: 13th-century Sun Temple — a UNESCO stone chariot in rock

why.winter: Best light on the Sun Temple's stone wheels, and December's Dance Festival draws top performers.
why.summer: Stone courtyards get scorching by midday — visit at dawn or skip Apr-Jun altogether.
why.monsoon: Humid and wet with little shade around the complex — an uncomfortable half-day visit.
why.autumn: Comfortable temperatures return by November — good timing to combine with Puri.

vibe: A half-day monument stop for most; stay overnight for December's dance festival.
hub: 35km/1hr from Puri by shared auto or bus; easy day trip.
festival: Dec: Konark Dance Festival

name: Puri
tagline: Jagannath Temple pilgrim town with a long, easy beach

why.winter: Best beach weather of the year — dry, cool sea breeze, comfortable for temples and sand alike.
why.summer: Apr-Jun heat is severe even by the coast; the sea offers little relief from the humidity.
why.monsoon: Rough surf and heavy rain most of the season, though Rath Yatra (Jun/Jul) draws huge crowds anyway.
why.autumn: Oct is warm but improving fast; by Nov it's comfortable and less crowded than December.

vibe: More pilgrims than backpackers, but easy day trips to Konark and Chilika keep it social.
hub: Direct train from Kolkata/Bhubaneswar; Puri has its own station.
festival: Jun-Jul: Rath Yatra

name: Pondicherry (incl. Auroville)
tagline: French Quarter beach town next to the Auroville commune

why.winter: Peak season - cool 20-29C, dry air, best for cycling the French Quarter and long beach walks
why.summer: Hot and humid (35C+), thin crowds, ashram and cafes still run but midday is rough going
why.monsoon: SW monsoon barely touches this coast - warm, muggy, occasional showers, decent value season
why.autumn: NE monsoon lands hard - Nov is the wettest month, rough seas, sudden downpours, best skipped

vibe: French Quarter cafes and Auroville draw a backpacker-yogi crowd, easy to meet people
hub: Fly/train to Chennai, 3hr drive; or train to Villupuram + bus
festival: Aug 15: Sri Aurobindo's birthday celebrations at the Ashram

name: Amritsar
tagline: The Golden Temple and its free kitchen for all
festival: Apr: Baisakhi at the Golden Temple

why.winter: Cold mornings at the Golden Temple are atmospheric, especially the pre-dawn Palki ceremony.
why.summer: Punjab plains heat hits past 40C, though the temple's marble floors stay cooling underfoot.
why.monsoon: Humid with heavy rain bursts, but the temple complex runs fully and is far less crowded.
why.autumn: Comfortable temperatures building toward Diwali, when the temple is spectacularly lit.

vibe: The Golden Temple's langar hall makes it genuinely easy to meet people.
hub: Fly into Amritsar (ATQ) or 6h train from Delhi/Chandigarh

name: Patiala
tagline: Royal Punjab — pegs, palaces and heritage gardens

why.winter: Comfortable weather for touring Qila Mubarak and the Sheesh Mahal grounds.
why.summer: Punjab plains heat is intense past 40C with rising humidity by May.
why.monsoon: Green parks and gardens, but heavy humidity makes the walking tour uncomfortable.
why.autumn: Mild and pleasant — a good shoulder-season stop between Delhi and Amritsar.

vibe: Almost no traveler infrastructure — you'll be sightseeing largely on your own.
hub: 1h train/bus from Chandigarh, or 4h from Delhi

name: Bharatpur (Keoladeo National Park)
tagline: India's top bird sanctuary, best seen by bicycle

why.winter: Peak birding season — migratory ducks, storks and raptors fill the wetlands.
why.summer: March is still pleasant, but by April-May the park dries out and heat tops 42C with little birdlife.
why.monsoon: June-July stay hot and dry; by August-September wetlands refill and breeding starts — a good, quiet window.
why.autumn: Migratory birds start arriving from Central Asia through October-November, building toward peak numbers.

vibe: Birders and cyclists share dirt paths — easy to strike up talk with fellow travelers.
hub: Train from Delhi (3.5h) or Agra (1.5h); explore by cycle-rickshaw

name: Bikaner
tagline: Remote desert city of camels and forts
festival: Jan: Bikaner Camel Festival

why.winter: The one genuinely pleasant season — cool days for the fort, camel farm and Karni Mata temple.
why.summer: Deep desert heat past 44C with dust storms; there's no upside to visiting now.
why.monsoon: Barely any rain reaches this far into the Thar, so the punishing heat just continues.
why.autumn: Temperatures fall through October and November, the desert turns bearable again.

vibe: Off the backpacker circuit — expect to explore the fort mostly on your own.
hub: Overnight train from Delhi (7-8h) or 5h bus from Jaipur

name: Bundi
tagline: Sleepy stepwell town, more fairytale than crowded
festival: Nov: Bundi Utsav

why.winter: Cool, quiet, ideal for wandering the palace and stepwells without crowds.
why.summer: Plains heat hits past 42C with little shade in the narrow lanes — best avoided.
why.monsoon: The town's famous stepwells fill dramatically and the surrounding hills turn green.
why.autumn: Temperatures ease and the post-monsoon countryside is at its greenest.

vibe: Quiet and unpolished; you'll mostly meet the same handful of travelers staying in town.
hub: 3h bus/train from Kota, or 5h from Jaipur

name: Chittorgarh
tagline: India's largest hill fort, steeped in siege history

why.winter: Cool enough to actually walk the fort's 13km perimeter in comfort.
why.summer: Exposed stone ramparts turn into an oven past 40C — a brutal midday walk.
why.monsoon: Green surroundings and dramatic light on the fort, though humidity makes the long walk sticky.
why.autumn: Warm but manageable, and the fort's ponds and stepwells are still full from the rains.

vibe: A day-trip town from Udaipur — quiet evenings, little traveler mixing.
hub: 2h train/bus from Udaipur, or 4h from Jaipur

name: Jaipur
tagline: Pink City gateway to Rajasthan's forts and bazaars
festival: Jan: Jaipur Literature Festival

why.winter: Peak season — crisp mornings, clear fort views, and the biggest crowds of the year.
why.summer: Brutal heat past 42C by April; sightsee only at dawn/dusk, or skip it entirely.
why.monsoon: Cooler and green with the Teej festival in August, though midday heat and humidity persist.
why.autumn: Warm days easing into pleasant nights — a good transition before the winter rush.

vibe: Hostel-heavy and social — easiest Rajasthan city to instantly find a travel group.
hub: Fly into Jaipur (Sanganer) or 4.5h train/bus from Delhi

name: Jaisalmer
tagline: Golden fort rising from the Thar dunes
festival: Feb: Jaisalmer Desert Festival

why.winter: Prime season — cold desert nights under the stars, comfortable dune safaris by day.
why.summer: Among India's hottest towns, past 45C with sandstorms; genuinely avoid this window.
why.monsoon: Rain is minimal but heat lingers through the monsoon months with zero relief.
why.autumn: Temperatures start dropping by late October, dune camps become bearable again.

vibe: Desert-camp bonfires and shared jeep safaris turn strangers into a travel crew fast.
hub: Overnight train from Jodhpur (5h) or fly direct into Jaisalmer

name: Jodhpur
tagline: Blue City beneath a clifftop fort
festival: Oct: Rajasthan International Folk Festival (RIFF)

why.winter: Cool, dry, and clear — the best time to walk the fort ramparts and blue-city lanes.
why.summer: Scorching past 42C; the thick fort walls help indoors, but street exploring is grim.
why.monsoon: Rain is light but heat and humidity together make walking the blue lanes exhausting.
why.autumn: Temperatures drop fast through October into a comfortably cool November, RIFF festival time.

vibe: Blue-lane guesthouses under the fort make it easy to fall into a group within a day.
hub: Fly into Jodhpur or 5h train from Jaipur

name: Kumbhalgarh
tagline: Fort behind the world's second-longest wall

why.winter: Best weather for the fort walls and the wildlife sanctuary's forest walks.
why.summer: Hot and dusty; the long uphill walk along the wall gets punishing by midday.
why.monsoon: Aravalli hills turn green and waterfalls appear, though the ghat road can get slick.
why.autumn: Pleasant and clear, with good visibility along the wall's full stretch.

vibe: Remote and resort-driven; you'll likely be the only solo guest most nights.
hub: 2h drive/taxi from Udaipur; no direct train

name: Mandawa (Shekhawati)
tagline: Open-air gallery of frescoed merchant havelis

why.winter: Ideal for walking between painted havelis all day without the desert sun wearing you down.
why.summer: Semi-arid plains heat is severe — nearby Churu has recorded some of India's hottest days.
why.monsoon: Heat lingers with little rain relief; not a rewarding season to be outdoors here.
why.autumn: Cooling off by November, with good soft light for photographing the painted facades.

vibe: Haveli homestays and painted-mansion walks; peaceful and quiet, not very social.
hub: 4h drive/bus from Jaipur or Delhi via Sikar

name: Mount Abu
tagline: Rajasthan's only hill station, oasis from the heat
festival: May: Mount Abu Summer Festival

why.winter: Clear skies but genuinely cold nights near freezing at Guru Shikhar — pack real layers.
why.summer: Peak season for a reason — the one hill station where plains-dwellers escape 45C heat.
why.monsoon: Waterfalls and viewpoints turn lush, but heavy fog can blank the famous sunset point for days.
why.autumn: Crowds thin out after summer and the weather turns comfortably mild.

vibe: Mostly Gujarati honeymooners and families around Nakki Lake; solo travelers stand out.
hub: Fly/train to Udaipur, then 2.5h taxi/bus up the ghat

name: Neemrana
tagline: 15th-century fort turned zipline weekend escape

why.winter: The classic season for the fort-palace terraces and zipline — cool, clear days.
why.summer: Plains heat makes the stone fort punishing by midday, pool and shade only go so far.
why.monsoon: A genuinely popular monsoon-getaway window — the valley below the fort turns green.
why.autumn: Warm but settling, with fewer weekend crowds than winter brings.

vibe: A Delhi-couples weekend crowd at the fort hotel; not built for solo mixing.
hub: 1.5h drive/bus from Delhi or Jaipur on NH48

name: Pushkar
tagline: Holy lake town, Rajasthan's backpacker capital
festival: Nov: Pushkar Camel Fair (Kartik Purnima)

why.winter: Cool lake mornings, full-moon aarti, and the Camel Fair crowd — this is peak Pushkar.
why.summer: Shadeless streets and 42C afternoons make the lake ghats unbearable by midday.
why.monsoon: Quiet and green with the lake replenished, though July heat lingers before real relief.
why.autumn: The Camel Fair in November draws huge crowds; October is calmer and still pleasant.

vibe: Lake-ghat cafes and yoga classes — one of India's easiest towns to travel solo.
hub: Fly/train to Ajmer, then 30min bus or auto

name: Ranakpur
tagline: Forest-valley home to a landmark Jain temple

why.winter: The marble temple's carvings photograph best in soft winter light.
why.summer: Very hot by midday, though the marble interior stays surprisingly cool underfoot.
why.monsoon: The surrounding forest valley turns vividly green — one of the region's prettier monsoon drives.
why.autumn: Clear skies and comfortable temperatures for the drive and temple visit.

vibe: A half-day temple stop, not a stay — barely any traveler scene to speak of.
hub: 1.5h drive from Udaipur, often combined with Kumbhalgarh

name: Ranthambore
tagline: Rajasthan's best shot at a wild tiger sighting

why.winter: Peak safari season — cool mornings and thinning grass make tiger sightings more reliable.
why.summer: Hot, but arguably the best sightings window — animals gather at shrinking waterholes as forests dry out.
why.monsoon: Closed 1 Jul-30 Sep for the breeding season; no safaris run, though June (still open) has superb sightings.
why.autumn: Reopens 1 October but tall post-monsoon grass keeps sighting odds lower until the grass dies back.

vibe: Couples and families on safari packages; evenings are resort-bound, not very social.
hub: Train to Sawai Madhopur (4.5h from Jaipur), taxi to park gate

name: Sariska Tiger Reserve
tagline: Former royal hunting ground, now a tiger reserve

why.winter: Best combination of cool, comfortable safaris and thinning vegetation for sightings.
why.summer: Hot, but animals cluster at shrinking waterholes, which can mean better tiger and leopard sightings.
why.monsoon: Core zone closed 1 Jul-30 Sep for the breeding season; safaris pause and June turns punishing anyway.
why.autumn: Reopens in October, but tall grass from the monsoon limits visibility until deeper winter.

vibe: Safari-lodge crowd is mostly domestic families; sociable at breakfast, not a hangout.
hub: 2.5h drive from Delhi or 1h from Alwar train station

name: Udaipur
tagline: City of Lakes — palaces and postcard sunsets
festival: Mar: Mewar Festival (Gangaur)

why.winter: Best weather of the year — lake boat rides and rooftop dinners without the sweat.
why.summer: Lakes shrink and heat climbs past 38C, though evenings by the water stay tolerable.
why.monsoon: Genuinely underrated — lakes fill, hills turn green, Sajjangarh's monsoon views are the year's best.
why.autumn: Post-monsoon lakes are full and the weather turns pleasant — arguably the best month to visit.

vibe: Lakeside rooftop cafes are full of backpackers swapping Rajasthan routes nightly.
hub: Fly into Udaipur or overnight train from Delhi/Jaipur

name: Gangtok
tagline: Sikkim's capital and gateway — monasteries, MG Marg cafés

why.winter: Cold but clear — good Kanchenjunga views on good days, North Sikkim trips possible if roads hold.
why.summer: Mar-Apr is peak (flower festival, clearest skies); by May haze builds ahead of the monsoon.
why.monsoon: Heavy rain and landslides regularly cut NH10 to the plains — the town's fine, travel isn't.
why.autumn: Post-monsoon clarity returns — the best combination of clear peaks and reliable road access.

vibe: Zostel crowd planning North Sikkim runs; easy to share permits and jeep seats.
hub: Fly Bagdogra, 4hr shared taxi; Indians need a free ILP.
festival: May: International Flower Festival

name: North Sikkim (Lachen-Lachung)
tagline: Yumthang valley and Gurudongmar Lake near the Tibet border

why.winter: Roads to Gurudongmar and Zero Point are often snowed shut — beautiful if open, a gamble if not.
why.summer: Apr-May is the sweet spot: Yumthang's 'valley of flowers' blooming, roads freshly reopened.
why.monsoon: Landslide season on single-lane mountain roads — this is when the region gets cut off for days.
why.autumn: Clear, cold and reliably open — the most dependable window for actually reaching Gurudongmar.

vibe: No independent travel - permits put you in an agent's shared jeep with strangers.
hub: From Gangtok, agent-booked permit and shared jeep required.

name: Pelling
tagline: Closest hotel-window views of Kanchenjunga in Sikkim

why.winter: Cold, clear mornings — reliable Kanchenjunga-from-bed views with a fraction of Gangtok's crowd.
why.summer: Mar-Apr brings the best light on the peaks; by May haze creeps in ahead of the rains.
why.monsoon: Persistent cloud erases the very views Pelling is famous for, plus landslide risk on approach roads.
why.autumn: The reliable window — the clearest Kanchenjunga views of the year, cool and comfortable.

vibe: Quieter than Gangtok - sunrise balconies, day trips to Khecheopalri lake.
hub: 4-5hr shared jeep from Gangtok or NJP via Jorethang.

name: Ravangla
tagline: Laid-back South Sikkim town under a 130ft Buddha statue

why.winter: Clear, cold mornings at Buddha Park — good light for the Kanchenjunga range from Tendong hill.
why.summer: Mar-Apr rhododendrons bloom around the park; pleasant before the pre-monsoon haze sets in.
why.monsoon: Cloud cover kills the panoramic views this town is built around; hill roads turn landslide-prone.
why.autumn: Best combination of clear skies and mild days — an easy, uncrowded stop between Gangtok and Pelling.

vibe: Quiet monastery town, far fewer tourists than Gangtok or Pelling - good for slow days.
hub: 3-4hr shared jeep from Gangtok, en route to Pelling.
festival: Aug-Sep: Pang Lhabsol at Ralang Monastery

name: Yuksom
tagline: Sikkim's first capital, trailhead for the Goecha La trek

why.winter: High passes are snowbound and the Goecha La trail is closed above Dzongri — town visits only.
why.summer: Apr-May is prime trekking: rhododendron blooms and clear Kanchenjunga views from Goecha La.
why.monsoon: Leeches, landslides and zero visibility at altitude — trek operators won't run departures.
why.autumn: The other prime window — crisp air and the clearest close-up views of Kanchenjunga's south face.

vibe: Trekkers gather before Dzongri/Goecha La; permits assign you a small trek group.
hub: 6-7hr drive from NJP/Bagdogra; permit via trek agent at check-post.

name: Zuluk
tagline: Zigzag Old Silk Route road through homestay-only villages

why.winter: Snow likely on the higher switchbacks — spectacular if the road's open, check status first.
why.summer: Mar-Apr is prime: clear zigzag-road views and blooming rhododendrons toward Nathang valley.
why.monsoon: Fog blankets the hairpins and landslides regularly shut this single-lane road — skip it.
why.autumn: The most reliable season — clear air for photographing the famous switchback road from above.

vibe: Homestay dinners, zero nightlife - you meet whoever's in your shared taxi.
hub: From Gangtok, permit + 4-5hr drive via Rongli; homestays only.

name: Chennai
tagline: Tamil Nadu's coastal capital - Marina Beach, transport hub

why.winter: The city's best season - Margazhi music season fills sabhas citywide, Marina walks are pleasant at dawn
why.summer: Brutally hot and humid, 40C+ with little relief even at night, best treated as a transit stop not a stay
why.monsoon: SW monsoon has limited effect here, hot and humid but liveable, workable for museums and day trips
why.autumn: NE monsoon lands hard - Nov-Dec brings the city's heaviest rain and occasional flooding, expect delays

vibe: A proper metro - hostels, easy transport, and backpackers passing through en route south
hub: Major airport (MAA) and rail hub - gateway to all of Tamil Nadu
festival: Dec-Jan: Margazhi Music Season - world's largest music festival

name: Chettinad (Karaikudi)
tagline: Nagarathar mansion towns, famed for architecture and cuisine

why.winter: Best months - cool enough to wander the huge Athangudi-tiled mansions and courtyards without plains heat
why.summer: Brutally hot interior plains climate, 38-40C, the vast mansion courtyards offer little shade at midday
why.monsoon: Hot and mostly dry (rain-shadow territory), humid discomfort rather than any real rain relief
why.autumn: NE monsoon brings moderate rain by Nov, greenery picks up, a decent trade-off with fewer visitors

vibe: A heritage and food pilgrimage; homestays let solo travellers settle in easily
hub: Fly to Madurai or Trichy, then 1.5-2hr drive/bus to Karaikudi

name: Coonoor
tagline: Quieter, lower Nilgiri twin to Ooty, ringed by tea estates

why.winter: Cool and clear, fewer fog days than Ooty, good for tea-estate walks without a jacket-in-the-mist fight
why.summer: Warm pleasant days among tea gardens, a quieter overflow alternative to a packed Ooty
why.monsoon: Wet and misty like the rest of the Nilgiris, Ghat sections prone to landslides after heavy spells
why.autumn: Post-monsoon clarity, tea estates glisten green, a calm low-key alternative to Ooty's Oct crowds

vibe: Sleepy tea-estate town, homestays over hostels - better for quiet solo walks than a crowd
hub: Fly to Coimbatore (70km, 2.5hr) or toy train from Mettupalayam

name: Kanyakumari
tagline: India's southern tip, where three seas meet at dawn and dusk

why.winter: Clearest skies of the year - the sunrise-over-Bay-of-Bengal, sunset-over-Arabian-Sea views actually deliver
why.summer: Hot and increasingly humid through Apr-May, haze often dulls the sunrise and sunset views
why.monsoon: SW monsoon spillover from the nearby Ghats brings rain and choppy seas, ferry to Vivekananda Rock often halts
why.autumn: Oct-Nov is the NE monsoon's peak here too - heaviest rain and roughest seas, the worst window to visit

vibe: A bucket-list stop with many day-trippers; budget lodges near the rock ease meeting others
hub: Fly to Trivandrum (90km, 1.5hr) or train from Madurai (4hr)

name: Kodaikanal
tagline: Misty Palani lake town loved by trekkers, backpackers

why.winter: Cold and often thickly foggy - Coaker's Walk views can vanish for days, but log-fire evenings compensate
why.summer: Warm days, cool nights, best visibility of the year - the classic escape-the-heat season, expect crowds
why.monsoon: Heavy rain and near-constant mist, Ghat road landslide risk, most viewpoints socked in - skip it
why.autumn: Skies clear after the rains, waterfalls run full, greenery peaks with fewer crowds than summer

vibe: Backpacker trekking hub - goStops hostel, bike rentals, easy to team up for treks
hub: Fly to Madurai (120km, 3hr) or train to Kodai Road + bus/taxi
festival: May: Kodaikanal Summer Festival (boat pageant, flower show)

name: Kolli Hills
tagline: Namakkal's plateau of hairpin bends, waterfalls, betel farms

why.winter: Cool, clear and quiet - good light for the Ghat's 70 hairpin bends and the Agaya Gangai waterfall trek
why.summer: Warmer and drier, waterfalls thin out by Apr-May, still noticeably cooler than the Namakkal plains below
why.monsoon: Heavy rain on the Ghat road with landslide risk, waterfalls run full but access can be cut after storms
why.autumn: Rains ease through Oct-Nov, the forest is lush and green, one of the quietest good-weather windows

vibe: Undiscovered by backpackers - a few eco-stays, ideal for solo travellers wanting quiet
hub: Nearest town Namakkal; the 70-hairpin Ghat road (1hr) from Semmedu

name: Madurai
tagline: Temple city built around the towering Meenakshi Amman Temple

why.winter: Best months - mornings cool enough for long temple walks, pleasant evenings by the Meenakshi tank
why.summer: Brutal - 40C+ by April-May, stone temple floors scorch bare feet by midday, only bearable dawn or dusk
why.monsoon: Dry and still hot (Madurai sits in a rain-shadow), 34-36C with humidity, not the SW monsoon's target zone
why.autumn: NE monsoon brings scattered evening showers by Nov, temperatures ease off, a decent trade-off season

vibe: Pilgrims and heritage travellers, not a party crowd; lodges near the temple ease day trips
hub: Fly direct to Madurai airport, or overnight train from Chennai (8hr)
festival: Apr-May: Chithirai Festival, Meenakshi's temple procession

name: Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram)
tagline: UNESCO shore temples and carvings on a laid-back beach strip

why.winter: Best window - cool evenings on the beach, comfortable for climbing over Krishna's Butterball all day
why.summer: Hot, glary and humid on the open rock terrain by Apr-May, best done in the early morning only
why.monsoon: Rain-shadow effect keeps this coast mostly dry through the SW monsoon, hot and humid but workable
why.autumn: NE monsoon rain picks up through Oct-Nov, rough surf, sudden downpours can wash out temple-hopping plans

vibe: A real backpacker beach vibe near Chennai - surf schools and cafes help you meet people
hub: 1hr drive/bus down the ECR from Chennai, frequent buses from CMBT
festival: Dec-Jan: Mahabalipuram Dance Festival at the Shore Temple

name: Ooty (Udhagamandalam)
tagline: Nilgiris' colonial hill capital, toy train and tea gardens

why.winter: Cold, clear mornings with frost near Doddabetta, pack warm layers, quieter after the New Year rush
why.summer: Peak hill-season crowds (Apr-May), pleasant 15-25C days, book ahead as plains tourists flood in
why.monsoon: Heavy SW monsoon - persistent rain, fog by noon, Ghat road landslide risk, best skipped
why.autumn: Oct is gorgeous - monsoon clears, tea gardens turn vivid green, thinner crowds than summer

vibe: More honeymooners than backpackers, but Zostel and the toy-train crowd help you link up
hub: Fly to Coimbatore (85km, 3hr) or train to Mettupalayam + toy train
festival: May: Ooty Summer Festival (flower and fruit show)

name: Rameswaram
tagline: Sacred island town at land's end - temple and Pamban Bridge

why.winter: Best months - cool sea breeze, calm seas for the Dhanushkodi drive, comfortable temple corridors
why.summer: Hot and glaring on the exposed sandy terrain, 36-38C, the temple's long stone corridors get scorching
why.monsoon: Dry season here (SW monsoon misses this coast), hot with a steady sea breeze, workable if heat-tolerant
why.autumn: NE monsoon and Bay of Bengal cyclone season - rough seas, Dhanushkodi road can flood, boats get cancelled

vibe: A pilgrim town at heart, but the Dhanushkodi ghost-town trip draws solo photographers
hub: Train/bus from Madurai (3hr) over the Pamban Bridge, or fly to Madurai
festival: Feb: Maha Shivaratri celebrations at Ramanathaswamy Temple

name: Thanjavur
tagline: Chola capital, home of the UNESCO Brihadeeswarar Temple

why.winter: Ideal - cool mornings for the temple complex and palace museum without the midday stone-floor heat
why.summer: Delta heat and humidity climb past 38C, temple visits only comfortable at opening or closing time
why.monsoon: Hot and muggy rather than wet (rain-shadow territory for the SW monsoon), no real relief yet
why.autumn: Nov is the wettest month here - Cauvery delta NE monsoon rain can flood low areas, wait for Dec

vibe: A quiet heritage stop, not a hangout town - mostly day-trippers and history buffs
hub: Train from Chennai (6hr) or fly to Trichy (65km) then bus/auto
festival: Feb: Thanjavur Music & Dance Festival at Brihadeeswarar Temple

name: Valparai
tagline: Remote Anamalai plateau of tea estates and wildlife

why.winter: Best season - clear skies, cool mornings, prime time to spot elephants, gaur and lion-tailed macaques
why.summer: Warm but tolerable given the altitude, tea estates green up, far fewer visitors than the big hill names
why.monsoon: One of Tamil Nadu's wettest patches - relentless rain, frequent landslides on the Ghat, best avoided
why.autumn: Rain tapers off through Oct-Nov, waterfalls run full, greenery peaks - a good transition window

vibe: Almost no backpacker scene - a few estate stays, best for solo travellers who like quiet
hub: Fly to Coimbatore, drive to Pollachi then the 40-hairpin Ghat road

name: Yelagiri
tagline: Small hill station near Bangalore-Chennai, minus Ooty crowds

why.winter: Cool, clear and quiet - the best months for the Punganur lake boat ride and the short Swamimalai trek
why.summer: Warm days draw Bangalore weekend crowds escaping plains heat, but it's mild hill warmth, not a true escape
why.monsoon: Rain picks up and viewpoints cloud over, roads can be slippery on the 14-hairpin Ghat approach
why.autumn: Skies clear post-monsoon by Oct, greenery is at its best, still fairly quiet outside weekends

vibe: A low-key weekend escape for Bangalore/Chennai crowds, not a backpacker circuit
hub: Nearest rail Jolarpettai (8km); self-drive 3.5hr from Bangalore
festival: May: Yelagiri Summer Festival (Tamil Nadu Tourism)

name: Hyderabad
tagline: Old-city bazaars, Golconda Fort, and biryani everywhere

why.winter: Best sightseeing weather - cool evenings for Charminar's night market and Golconda's show.
why.summer: Dry heat past 40C by April-May; the old city's crowded lanes get oppressive by midday.
why.monsoon: Moderate rain cools things down, the lakes fill up, though heavy spells snarl traffic.
why.autumn: October onward is the turning point - heat breaks, air clears, best months of the year.

vibe: Growing hostel and cafe scene, huge student/IT crowd - easy to find company.
hub: Major international airport (HYD) with direct flights nationwide.
festival: Jul-Aug: Bonalu, Telangana's signature folk festival for Mahakali

name: Warangal
tagline: Kakatiya temple capital, gateway to UNESCO's Ramappa

why.winter: Coolest, clearest months for the fort, Thousand Pillar Temple, and the Ramappa day trip.
why.summer: Interior heat past 40C by April-May, little shade at the exposed ruins - go early morning.
why.monsoon: Moderate rain, the temples and Bhadrakali lake turn green, heat backs off noticeably.
why.autumn: October-November brings clear skies for the full Kakatiya heritage circuit.

vibe: A quiet day-trip circuit for history buffs - easy alone, but not much of a social scene.
hub: 2.5-3h train or bus from Hyderabad; Ramappa a further 1.5h taxi.
festival: Jan: Medaram Jatara (Sammakka-Saralamma), biennial tribal fair

name: Agartala & Unakoti
tagline: Palace capital plus giant rock-cut carvings at Unakoti

why.winter: Best time — cool and dry for Ujjayanta Palace and the day trip out to Unakoti's carvings.
why.summer: March-April is warm but manageable; May turns hot and humid before the rains.
why.monsoon: Heavy, sustained rain; Unakoti's forest trail turns slippery and leech-prone.
why.autumn: October cools down quickly, big Durga Puja energy as the rains taper off.

vibe: Overlooked capital — often the only visitor at Unakoti's carvings.
hub: Fly to Agartala; Unakoti is 3-4h drive via Kailashahar. No ILP.
festival: Jul: Kharchi Puja, Tripura's major traditional festival

name: Agra
tagline: The Taj Mahal and Mughal monuments, UP's biggest draw

why.winter: Peak season — cool, clear days are ideal for the Taj, though January fog can delay sunrise views
why.summer: April-June plains heat hits 45C+; walking the marble courtyards at midday is genuinely dangerous
why.monsoon: Humid but the rains green the gardens and thin the crowds — an underrated window if you handle the stickiness
why.autumn: Excellent weather returns by late October — comfortable temperatures, build-up to peak season

vibe: Taj Ganj guesthouses cluster travelers together, though touts can be relentless
hub: Gatimaan/Shatabdi Express from Delhi 1h45m, or drive 3.5h
festival: Feb: Taj Mahotsav

name: Ayodhya
tagline: Rama's birthplace, home to the newly built Ram Mandir

why.winter: Peak pilgrimage season — comfortable weather for the temple circuit and river ghats
why.summer: Heat climbs fast by April-May; Ram Navami in April draws huge crowds despite the temperature
why.monsoon: Humid and less crowded, the Saryu ghats are atmospheric but expect rain disruptions
why.autumn: Deepotsav in October/November is the single biggest draw — book accommodation months ahead

vibe: Overwhelmingly a pilgrim crowd post-Ram Mandir — here for the temple, not socializing
hub: New Ayodhya airport direct flights, or train from Lucknow 2h
festival: Oct/Nov: Deepotsav lamp festival

name: Lucknow
tagline: Nawabi capital of grand Imambaras and kebabs

why.winter: Best season — comfortable for walking through Bara Imambara and the old-city food lanes
why.summer: April-June heat is severe and exploring the old quarters on foot becomes a real chore
why.monsoon: Humid and occasionally waterlogged streets, but indoor monuments and markets stay enjoyable
why.autumn: Weather turns pleasant by late October, a good time to explore before winter's peak crowds

vibe: More food-and-heritage city than backpacker hub — solo dining beats meeting travelers
hub: Flights or train from Delhi 6-7h; well connected by air

name: Varanasi
tagline: Ancient Ganges ghats, India's chaotic spiritual heart

why.winter: Peak season — cool mornings for sunrise boat rides, and Dev Deepawali in November is unmissable
why.summer: Brutal 45C+ heat with high humidity by May-June; the ghats are near-empty for good reason
why.monsoon: The Ganges rises and can submerge lower ghat steps; muggy but atmospheric if you handle the heat
why.autumn: Pleasant temperatures return by late October, building to the spectacular Dev Deepawali festival

vibe: Long-term travelers linger for weeks on the ghats; boat-sharing makes solo mixing easy
hub: Flights/trains from Delhi 12h; airport 25km from the ghats
festival: Nov: Dev Deepawali

name: Vrindavan-Mathura
tagline: Krishna's birthplace and playground of temple towns

why.winter: Peak season — cool enough for long temple-hopping days across Vrindavan's 1000+ temples
why.summer: Severe heat by April-May; only the devout brave the midday sun for temple visits
why.monsoon: Humid and quieter — a good off-peak window if the spiritual pull outweighs sticky weather
why.autumn: Excellent weather resumes by late October, with Diwali on Krishna's home turf drawing crowds

vibe: ISKCON's international devotees give this temple town a surprisingly easy-to-meet vibe
hub: Train Delhi to Mathura 2-3h, then auto to Vrindavan 15km
festival: Mar: Holi, incl. Barsana's Lathmar Holi

name: Almora
tagline: Understated Kumaoni market town with Himalayan views

why.winter: Cold, clear mornings and snow-dusted peaks from Bright End Corner, but cafes shut early
why.summer: Warm days, cool nights — a calmer, cheaper alternative to Nainital's summer crowds
why.monsoon: Landslide-prone hill roads and low visibility erase the Himalayan views that are the point
why.autumn: Best light of the year — crisp air, snow-capped Trishul and Nanda Devi visible from town

vibe: Quiet old bazaar; the real traveler scene is a short ride away in Kasar Devi's hostels
hub: Rail Kathgodam 90km, 3h shared taxi; or overnight Delhi bus 9-10h

name: Auli
tagline: Uttarakhand's top ski slopes with Nanda Devi views

why.winter: Peak season — Uttarakhand's best skiing, snow slopes backed by views of Nanda Devi
why.summer: Green meadows and cable car views without snow — pleasant, but skiing, the main draw, is gone
why.monsoon: The Joshimath approach road is landslide-prone and views fog out completely — skip it
why.autumn: Clear and quiet before the snow arrives — good for the cable car, no skiing yet though

vibe: Ski instructors and Delhi weekenders; here for slopes and cable car, not nightlife
hub: Fly Dehradun 280km or train Rishikesh, then 9-10h via Joshimath
festival: Jan: Auli Winter Games

name: Binsar
tagline: Quiet oak sanctuary with 200km Himalayan views

why.winter: Cold and occasionally snowy, oak forest is stark and beautiful, but interior roads can be tricky
why.summer: Pleasant and cool, good birdwatching season before the rains, moderate crowds
why.monsoon: Leeches, mud, and landslide-prone approach roads make this best avoided in the rains
why.autumn: Clearest views of the year, dry trails, peak season for the 200km Himalayan panorama

vibe: Near-silent forest — you'll likely have the trails and rest house to yourself
hub: Rail Kathgodam 120km, 4h taxi via Almora; no public bus inside

name: Chakrata
tagline: Restricted cantonment near Delhi, untouched forest and falls

why.winter: Cold and often snowy above 2000m, roads to higher points like Deoban can close after heavy snow
why.summer: Pleasant, forested, and still nearly empty of tourists — a genuine off-the-radar escape
why.monsoon: Landslide-prone forest roads and a dangerously slippery Tiger Falls trail
why.autumn: Clear, dry, and the best time for the Tiger Falls hike and Deoban forest walks

vibe: Barely visited even by Indian tourists — likely the only outsider at Tiger Falls
hub: Train Dehradun 90km, 3h taxi; foreigners need prior permission

name: Chopta
tagline: Basecamp for the Tungnath-Chandrashila alpine trek

why.winter: Snow trekking to Chandrashila draws a niche crowd, but it's bitterly cold with tricky footing
why.summer: Prime trekking season — wildflower meadows, clear alpine views, good trail conditions
why.monsoon: Leeches, slippery trails, and landslide-hit approach roads make this the worst window to trek
why.autumn: Post-monsoon skies are clearest of the year — arguably the best trekking weather here

vibe: Trekkers swap trail stories in tiny dhabas — small but genuine traveler community
hub: Taxi/bus from Rishikesh or Haridwar 7-8h via Rudraprayag

name: Kausani
tagline: 300km Himalayan skyline view, Gandhi's hill retreat

why.winter: Clearest Himalayan panorama of the year — snow peaks framed against clear skies, cold but worth it
why.summer: Pleasant and green in March-April; May warms up but stays a calmer escape than Nainital
why.monsoon: Clouds hide the entire reason to visit — the mountain view — plus landslide risk en route
why.autumn: Post-monsoon clarity makes this peak season for the panoramic view Kausani is famous for

vibe: Mostly honeymooners chasing sunrise views; solo travelers may find few peers here
hub: Rail Kathgodam 135km, then 4-5h taxi via Almora; no direct air/rail

name: Kedarnath
tagline: Himalayan Shiva shrine at 3583m, open just 6 months

why.winter: Closed entirely — the temple shuts around early November and the deity moves to Ukhimath
why.summer: May-June is prime pilgrimage season before the monsoon; trails are clear, temple newly reopened
why.monsoon: Technically open but this is landslide and flash-flood country — the 2013 disaster hit in this window
why.autumn: September-October is the second great window — thinning crowds, temple closes by early November

vibe: Shoulder-to-shoulder with pilgrims on the climb — devotion, not a party circuit
hub: Bus/taxi to Sonprayag 9-10h, jeep to Gaurikund, 16km trek or heli
festival: Apr/May: Kapat opening ceremony

name: Lansdowne
tagline: Sleepy Garhwal Rifles cantonment, refreshingly untouristy

why.winter: Cold, foggy mornings, occasional light snow — quiet and atmospheric, some cafes shut
why.summer: Cool pine-forest air, a favorite quick escape from Delhi's heat without Mussoorie's crowds
why.monsoon: Heavy rain and slippery forest trails; the cantonment turns genuinely gloomy and overgrown
why.autumn: Clear skies and comfortable temperatures — the best weather window of the year

vibe: Empty pine roads and military-town hush — solitude more than social mixing
hub: Train to Kotdwar 40km, then 1.5h taxi or shared jeep up

name: Mukteshwar
tagline: Laid-back orchard town with cliff views and paragliding

why.winter: Cold, clear, occasional snow — great for cozy homestays and unbroken Himalayan views
why.summer: Pleasant weather and the peak season for paragliding and rock climbing here
why.monsoon: Green and dramatic cloud views, but slippery cliffs raise the risk for outdoor activities
why.autumn: Crisp, clear, and quieter than summer — arguably the best all-round window

vibe: Weekend paragliders from Delhi/Bengaluru; friendly, not much of a hostel scene
hub: Rail Kathgodam 50km, 2h taxi; easy day trip from Nainital

name: Munsiyari
tagline: Remote gateway to Panchachuli peaks and glacier treks

why.winter: Snowbound and beautiful in December, but January-February often cuts off roads and shuts guesthouses
why.summer: April-May is prime trekking season; March is still cold as roads reopen after winter
why.monsoon: June is calm before the storm; July-September bring landslides that regularly cut the remote road
why.autumn: October is prime — post-monsoon clarity gives the best Panchachuli views; November turns cold fast

vibe: A trekking basecamp of serious hikers; guesthouse owners become your main company
hub: Fly Kathgodam, then 8-9h drive via Almora; shared jeeps run

name: Mussoorie
tagline: Colonial 'Queen of the Hills', Delhi's easiest escape

why.winter: Cold and foggy, occasional snow draws a niche crowd, but many cafes shut for the season
why.summer: Peak season — Delhi's classic heat escape, great weather but Mall Road gets packed
why.monsoon: Heavy rain and landslide-prone roads from Dehradun make the hillside genuinely risky
why.autumn: Best all-round window — clear skies, comfortable temperatures, fewer crowds than summer

vibe: Honeymooners throng Mall Road; solo travelers drift to quieter Landour nearby
hub: Fly/train Dehradun 35km, then 1h taxi up the hill

name: Nainital
tagline: Colonial lake town, Kumaon's biggest tourist magnet

why.winter: Cold, sometimes snowy — pretty around the lake but many hotels half-shut, mornings misty
why.summer: Peak crowds fleeing plains heat; book ahead, expect queues for the boat ride
why.monsoon: Frequent landslides on the approach roads and leeches on trails — best skipped
why.autumn: Clear skies, quieter lanes, and the best mountain views of the year

vibe: Boating families crowd the lake; solo travelers escape to quieter Naina Peak trails
hub: Rail Kathgodam 35km or overnight Delhi bus 7-8h to town
festival: Sep: Nanda Devi Mela

name: Rishikesh
tagline: Yoga capital and rafting hub on the Ganges

why.winter: Cool crisp days, clear Himalayan views from Kunjapuri, yoga ashrams at their calmest
why.summer: March is pleasant, but April-May heat climbs fast and the ghats fill with day-trippers
why.monsoon: Ganges swells brown and dangerous, rafting suspended, landslide risk on the Badrinath road
why.autumn: Best window of the year — rafting resumes, skies clear, the whole backpacker scene wakes up

vibe: Zostel dorms full of backpackers doing yoga by day, riverside chai by night
hub: Fly Dehradun 35km or overnight Delhi bus 6-7h; local auto-rickshaw
festival: Mar: International Yoga Festival

name: Valley of Flowers
tagline: UNESCO alpine meadow of rare flora, open Jul-Sep only

why.winter: Completely closed — the park and trek route are buried under snow from October to May
why.summer: Still closed; snowmelt is only beginning and the trail isn't passable until June at earliest
why.monsoon: The only real window — park opens in June but flowers aren't out yet; peak bloom is Jul-Aug, fading by mid-Sep
why.autumn: Closes by early October as snow returns — at most the first days are viable, don't risk it

vibe: Trekkers and Hemkund Sahib pilgrims share the trail — good camaraderie in Ghangaria
hub: Drive Rishikesh to Govindghat 10h, trek 14km to Ghangaria (permit)

name: Darjeeling
tagline: Queen of the Hills - tea, toy train, Kanchenjunga views

why.winter: Crisp, clear Kanchenjunga views most mornings; cold nights near freezing, pack real layers.
why.summer: Mar-Apr is peak: rhododendrons bloom and skies are clearest, but it's crowded — book ahead.
why.monsoon: Landslide season on the hill roads — the town itself is wet and foggy, views vanish for days.
why.autumn: Best window of the year: post-monsoon clarity, Kanchenjunga visible daily, Puja-season crowds.

vibe: Backpacker cafés on Nehru Road; easy to link a Sikkim loop or Sandakphu trek.
hub: Fly Bagdogra, 3hr jeep up; or NJP rail for the toy train.

name: Kalimpong
tagline: Quiet hill town near Darjeeling - monasteries, nurseries

why.winter: Cold and clear like Darjeeling but a fraction of the tourists — good for quiet monastery walks.
why.summer: Mar-Apr flower nurseries (Kalimpong supplies orchids nationwide) are in full, fragrant bloom.
why.monsoon: Same landslide risk as the rest of the Darjeeling hills — Teesta valley roads can shut suddenly.
why.autumn: Clear skies, cool air — the easiest month to combine with a Darjeeling or Sikkim loop.

vibe: Slower than Darjeeling, fewer backpackers - good for a quiet reset.
hub: Bagdogra airport or NJP rail, then 1.5-2hr taxi/jeep.

name: Kolkata
tagline: India's cultural capital - colonial streets, great food

why.winter: Best months in the city — cool, dry, Puja afterglow still in the air, easy all-day sightseeing.
why.summer: Apr-Jun is genuinely brutal: 40C+ with punishing humidity before the rains break — indoor days.
why.monsoon: Waterlogged streets after heavy downpours and high humidity throughout, though the food never stops.
why.autumn: Durga Puja (Oct) is the city's single best reason to visit — pandal-hopping, all-night energy.

vibe: Hostel common rooms, street-food crawls, easy to meet fellow backpackers.
hub: Major air/rail hub; direct flights and trains nationwide.
festival: Oct: Durga Puja

name: Mandarmani-Tajpur
tagline: Bengal's 'drive-on' beach — long flat sand, low-key escape

why.winter: Prime beach weather — dry and breezy, good for the famous bike-on-the-sand rides.
why.summer: Hot and increasingly humid through May as the Bay of Bengal builds toward monsoon.
why.monsoon: Rough surf, frequent rain and real cyclone risk off the Bay of Bengal — not a beach window.
why.autumn: Oct is still a bit unsettled post-monsoon; by Nov sea and weather have properly calmed.

vibe: Weekend crowd of Kolkata twenty-somethings, beach shacks and bonfires.
hub: 3hr drive/bus from Kolkata via Digha Road.

name: Sandakphu
tagline: West Bengal's highest point - sunrise over 4 of 5 top peaks

why.winter: Doable with proper gear — sub-zero nights and snow underfoot, but the clearest sunrise of the year.
why.summer: Apr rhododendrons carpet the ridge red and pink; by May haze builds as monsoon approaches.
why.monsoon: Leech-and-landslide trail with zero summit visibility — operators won't run departures.
why.autumn: Peak window: driest air of the year, both Everest and Kanchenjunga visible from one ridge.

vibe: Teahouse trek, trekkers worldwide; a mandatory guide means you're never truly alone.
hub: Base in Darjeeling; jeep to Manebhanjan, guide compulsory.

name: Sundarbans
tagline: World's largest mangrove forest — tiger territory by boat

why.winter: The real season here — calm water, cool air, best odds of spotting a tiger on the riverbanks.
why.summer: Apr-May heat and humidity in the delta are punishing, and tiger activity near the banks drops.
why.monsoon: Core-zone tourism effectively shuts — swollen rivers and unsafe boat conditions.
why.autumn: Oct is a reasonable early option as the water calms; Nov onward is noticeably better.

vibe: Little solo scene - most join a shared boat tour and bond over 3 days.
hub: 2hr drive from Kolkata to Godkhali jetty, then boat in.
